story.石油危機，{油價和米價一起漲，|什麼都在漲，}{家裡的菜錢不夠用了。|媽媽開始算: The world oil crisis reached Taiwan: {petrol and rice went up together,|everything went up,} {and the money for the family’s food no longer stretched far enough.|and Mum started counting every coin at the market.}

story.那年四月，蔣中正過世，{大家都配戴著黑紗。|電視台停播了娛樂節目。}: That April, President Chiang Kai-shek died. {Everyone wore a black mourning band.|The TV stations took their entertainment shows off the air.}

story.政府開放出國觀光，你跟著旅行團去了{日本|香港|泰國}，{第一次坐飛機，緊張得一: The government finally let ordinary people travel abroad as tourists, and you joined a tour group to {Japan|Hong Kong|Thailand}. {On your first ever flight, you gripped the armrest the whole way.|The souvenirs you brought back made the neighbours envious for ages.}

story.「大家樂」簽賭風靡全台，同事們天天在研究明牌。: “Everybody’s Happy”, an illegal numbers game riding on the national lottery’s results, has swept Taiwan, and your co-workers study “lucky numbers” every day.
story.巷口雜貨店的老闆偷偷在收大家樂的簽單，鄰居一個接一個去簽。: The owner of the corner shop is quietly taking bets for “Everybody’s Happy”, the illegal numbers game, and the neighbours drop in one after another.

story.解嚴的那個夏天，{你在電視上看著新聞，覺得有什麼不一樣了。|家裡的長輩聊天聊到很: The summer martial law ended, {you watched the news on TV and felt that something had changed.|the older folks at home talked late into the night.}

story.股市從一萬兩千多點崩到兩千多點，{你跟著大家買的股票套牢了。|號子裡有人當場哭出: The stock market crashed from over 12,000 points to just over 2,000. {The shares you had bought along with everyone else were stuck deep under water.|At the brokerage, someone burst into tears on the spot.}
story.那年股市大崩盤，{帳面上的錢少了一大半。|你發誓再也不聽明牌。}: That year Taiwan’s stock market collapsed. {More than half your money on paper was gone.|You swore never again to buy on a hot tip.}

story.全民健保開辦，{看醫生只要付掛號費，|爸媽終於肯去看拖了很久的病，}{大家都說這: National Health Insurance began, covering everyone. {Seeing a doctor now cost only a small registration fee,|Your parents finally saw a doctor about problems they had put off for years,} {and everyone said it was a good thing.|and you tucked your health card into your wallet.}
story.那年三月第一次總統直選，{你拿著身分證去投票，|全家一起去投票所，}{排隊時心裡: That March, Taiwan held its first direct presidential election. {You took your ID card and went to vote,|The whole family went to the polling station together,} {and your heart beat a little faster in the queue.|and after stamping your ballot you took a good look at the red ink on your finger.}
story.九二一大地震那晚，{家裡的牆裂了一條大縫，|整棟房子搖得像要倒下來，}全家人{抱: On the night of the 921 earthquake, the great quake of 21 September 1999, {a wide crack split the wall at home,|the whole house shook as if it would come down,} and the family {ran out to open ground clutching their quilts,|slept in the car for several nights,} {while the aftershocks kept coming.|only daring to go back for their things after daybreak.}
story.九二一大地震那晚，{你被搖醒，|停電了，}{整晚聽著收音機裡的消息。|第二天，全: On the night of the 921 earthquake, the great quake of 21 September 1999, {you were shaken awake|the power went out}, {and you listened to the radio news all night.|and the next day all of Taiwan watched the news from the middle of the island.}
story.九二一大地震後，{你捐了一些錢和物資到災區。|公司組隊去中部幫忙清理。}: After the 921 earthquake of September 1999, {you sent some money and supplies to the disaster area.|your company sent a team to central Taiwan to help clear up.}
story.納莉颱風把台北淹成一片，{捷運站變成水池，|騎樓的水淹到膝蓋，}{你停課停班了好: Typhoon Nari left Taipei under water: {MRT stations turned into pools,|the water under the shopfront arcades came up to your knees,} {and school and work were called off for days.|and when it drained away, the streets were piled with soaked furniture.}
story.SARS 爆發，你在醫院上班，{穿著悶熱的防護衣值班，|好幾個星期不敢回家，}{: When SARS broke out in Taiwan, you were working at a hospital. {You worked your shifts in a stifling protective suit,|For weeks you did not dare go home,} {and your family phoned every day to ask if you were all right.|and it was the most frightening, and the proudest, time of your life.}

story.那年跨年，台北 101 第一次放煙火，{你和朋友在信義區擠了好幾個小時，|你在電: That New Year’s Eve, Taipei 101, then the world’s tallest building, put on its first fireworks show. {You and your friends squeezed into the crowds in Xinyi for hours,|You counted down in front of the TV,} {and the fireworks burst out of the tower floor by floor.|and everyone screamed together.}
story.卡債風暴那幾年，{你的信用卡和現金卡越刷越多，|一張卡繳另一張卡，}{每個月的利: In the years of Taiwan’s credit-card debt crisis, {you ran up more and more on your credit and cash cards,|you paid off one card with another,} {and the interest alone ate more than half your pay each month.|and the banks’ collection calls left you afraid to answer your phone.}
story.高鐵通車了，{你第一次只花一個半小時就從北部到了高雄。|回老家的時間少了一大半。: The High Speed Rail opened. {For the first time you got from the north to Kaohsiung in an hour and a half.|The trip back to your hometown took less than half as long.} {You watched the rice fields fly past the window.|You arrived before you had finished your lunch box.}
story.金融海嘯，公司開始放無薪假，{你一個月只上兩個星期的班。|薪水少了一截，你開始帶: When the global financial crisis hit, your company began sending people on unpaid leave. {You worked only two weeks a month.|With your pay cut, you started bringing lunch from home.}

story.那年三月，立法院外面聚集了很多學生，{你的同學有人去了現場，有人在網路上看直播。: That March, crowds of students gathered outside the Legislative Yuan, Taiwan’s parliament. {Some of your classmates went in person; others watched the livestream.|Everyone in class was talking about it.} {You went to see it once yourself,|You watched the livestream all night in your dorm,} {and you would remember that spring.|and for those few weeks the campus felt different.}

story.除夕前的地震，{你在凌晨被搖醒，|整棟樓晃了好久，}{隔天看到新聞，倒塌的大樓就: The earthquake that struck just before Lunar New Year’s Eve: {you were shaken awake before dawn,|your building swayed for a long time,} {and the next day’s news showed the collapsed tower block was not far away.|and that year’s New Year’s Eve dinner was a quiet one.}
story.台北世大運那個夏天，{你買票去看了一場比賽，|你在電視前看了好多場比賽，}{跟著: The summer Taipei hosted the World University Games, {you bought a ticket to watch an event,|you watched event after event on TV,} {cheering along with the whole crowd.|and when a Taiwanese athlete won gold, you nearly cried.}
story.公教年金改革上路，{你的退休金每個月少了一些，|你重新算了一次退休後的開銷，}{: The pension reform for civil servants and teachers took effect. {Your monthly pension shrank a little,|You worked out your retirement budget all over again,} {and it was all anyone talked about when you met old colleagues.|and decided to live a little more frugally.}
story.五月，同性婚姻專法通過。{你和{partner}在電視前看著新聞，紅了眼眶。|你: In May, Taiwan passed its same-sex marriage law, the first in Asia. {You and {partner} watched the news on TV with tears in your eyes.|You and {partner} held each other tight in the crowd outside the Legislative Yuan.} At last, you could marry too.
story.五月，同性婚姻專法通過，{新聞上，第一批登記的新人在戶政事務所前合照。|你的同事: In May, Taiwan passed its same-sex marriage law, the first in Asia. {On the news, the first couples to register posed for photos outside the registry offices.|A co-worker told you happily that he could finally marry his partner of ten years.}

story.四月三日早上的大地震，{花蓮的房子搖到傾斜，|你家的櫃子全倒了，}{你們在操場的: In the big earthquake on the morning of 3 April, {buildings in Hualien were left leaning,|every cabinet in your home toppled over,} {and your family lived in a tent on a school field for days.|and landslides cut the mountain road through Taroko Gorge in several places.}
